# PIANISTpy

> PIANISTpy builds equilibrium models of spherical systems with a chosen velocity anisotropy: distribution functions by analytic inversion, truncation in phase space, particle initial conditions, line-of-sight observables, superposition and a differentiable likelihood. Python, JAX.

Every page of the manual has a markdown twin at the same address with
`.md` in place of `.html`; the whole manual as one file is
/docs/llms-full.txt.

## Documentation

- [Get started: what the package does, installation, quick start and representative computing time](https://pianistpy.com/docs/start/overview.md)
- [User guide: one page per topic](https://pianistpy.com/docs/guide/index.md)
- [Flags and refusals: what the package returns, flags and refuses](https://pianistpy.com/docs/guide/flags-refusals.md)
- [Examples: tutorial notebooks and the result figures of Chiang+(2026d)](https://pianistpy.com/docs/notebooks/index.md)
- [Functions by subpackage: the API reference](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/api/index.md)
- [Technical notes](https://pianistpy.com/docs/reference/notes.md)
- [How to cite](https://pianistpy.com/docs/project/citing.md)
